title: Dative 3: 'I Like It' (Нравится)
description: The 'нравится' construction puts the LIKER in the dative and the LIKED THING in the nominative. Today drills the dative personal pronouns and verb agreement.
descriptionRussian: Конструкция 'нравится' ставит того, кому нравится, в дательный падеж, а то, что нравится, — в именительный.
intro: Russian does not have a verb for 'to like'. It has a verb meaning roughly 'to be pleasing', and the sentence gets built the other way around: the thing you like becomes the subject and you become the recipient. So the music is doing the work and you are standing there receiving it. Get this one construction and a great deal of everyday Russian opens up.
rules: Нравиться means 'to be pleasing.' The LIKER goes in the DATIVE; the LIKED THING is the NOMINATIVE SUBJECT.
Dative personal pronouns: я → мне, ты → тебе, он → ему, она → ей, оно → ему, мы → нам, вы → вам, они → им.
The verb agrees with the SUBJECT (the liked thing). Singular subject → нравится. Plural subject → нравятся.
examples: Мне нравится музыка. (I like music.) Liker мне (dat); subject музыка (nom sg) → verb нравится.
Маше нравится фильм. (Masha likes the film.) Liker Маше (dat); subject фильм (nom sg) → нравится.
Нам нравятся песни. (We like the songs.) Liker нам (dat); subject песни (nom pl) → нравятся.
Антону нравится спорт. (Anton likes sport.) Liker Антону (dat); subject спорт (nom sg) → нравится.
Им нравится Москва. (They like Moscow.) Liker им (dat); subject Москва (nom sg) → нравится.

items.promptEnglish: I'm giving the book to brother.
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 2: the recipient of давать takes which case?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 2: verbs of giving take a dative recipient. Брат → брату. Today's lesson keeps the dative but uses a different construction: нравиться, where the liker is dative.

items.hint: Which form of 'я' is the dative?
items.explanation: Нравиться puts the liker in the dative. The dative of я is мне. Note that English uses 'I' (subject), but Russian uses мне (dative). The liker is not the grammatical subject in Russian; the LIKED thing (музыка) is the subject.

items.hint: Which form of 'ты' is the dative?
items.explanation: The dative of ты is тебе. Same construction as Q1.2 with a different liker. The verb is нравится because фильм is singular.

items.hint: Which form of 'мы' is the dative? Notice the verb is нравятся (plural).
items.explanation: The dative of мы is нам. Pay attention to the verb: песни is plural, so the verb is нравятся (plural). The liker (нам) and the verb agreement are independent: liker is dative; verb agrees with the liked thing.

items.hint: Which form of 'она' is the dative?
items.explanation: The dative of она is ей. Москва is singular, so the verb stays нравится.

items.hint: Which form of 'он' is the dative?
items.explanation: The dative of он is ему. Спорт is singular, so the verb is нравится.

items.hint: The liker goes in the dative; the liked thing is the nominative subject.
items.explanation: With нравиться the liker stands in the dative: Лене нравится музыка ('music is pleasing to Lena'). Feminine -а swaps to -е: Лена → Лене.

items.hint: Same frame: who does the liking, and what case do they take?
items.explanation: The liker takes the dative: Маше нравится фильм. The film is the nominative subject and the verb agrees with it.

items.hint: Песни is plural. What does the verb agree with?
items.explanation: The verb agrees with the liked thing, not the liker. Песни is plural, so нравятся: Антону нравятся песни.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: The LIKED thing is the nominative subject of нравиться. So фильм stays in its dictionary form. The dative liker (Маше) is what shifts; the subject does not.

errorCorrection.explanation: Нравиться does not work like English 'like'. It means 'to be pleasing to': the liker goes in the dative and the liked thing is the nominative subject. So the liker is мне (dative of я), not я: 'Мне нравится музыка' (literally 'to me is pleasing music'). The verb agrees with музыка, staying нравится.

With нравиться the verb agrees with the liked thing (the nominative subject), not the liker. The subject книги is plural, so the verb is нравятся (3pl), not нравится (3sg). The liker Антону stays dative regardless. Plural subject, plural verb: нравятся.

With нравиться the liked thing is the nominative subject, not an object: it is музыка, not музыку. Learners use музыку because любить ('to love') takes the accusative ('Маша любит музыку'), but нравиться flips the structure: the liker Маше is dative and the thing музыка is the nominative subject. The verb нравится agrees with музыка.

minimalPairs.explanation: Нравиться takes a dative liker. The dative of я is мне. The form меня (gen/acc) is wrong here; it would mean 'me' as a direct object, not as the liker.
The verb agrees with the SUBJECT (the liked thing). Песни is plural, so the verb is нравятся. If the subject were singular (e.g., песня), the verb would be нравится.

reviewVocab.definition: to be pleasing to (the liker is dative; the liked thing is the nominative subject)
is pleasing (sg) / are pleasing (pl); the verb agrees with the liked thing, not the liker
reviewVocab.example: Мне нравится фильм. Мне нравятся фильмы.

reviewVocab.definition: to love (takes the accusative, not the dative; contrasts with нравиться)
reviewVocab.example: Я люблю музыку. = Мне нравится музыка.
